newsitem.title: USA: Sharper Image loss widens in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Sharper Image loss widens in third quarter.

text.p: Sharper Image Corp. said Tuesday its losses rose sharply in the third quarter as high paper prices forced the retailer of gifts and products to curb its catalogue advertising, resulting in weaker sales.

Net losses widened to $1.7 million,or 20 cents a share, in the quarter ended Oct. 31, from $835,000, or 10 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Revenues fell 5 percent to $39.4 million from $41.3 million.
Comparable store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, slid 12 percent to $24.5 million from $27.7 million.

"Sales for the third quarter were affected by the lower number of catalogue pages circulated during the quarter as compared with the prior year," said Richard Thalheimer, founder and chairman of the company.

"Advertising expense was 22 percent lower than last year's same period, due primarily to fewer catalogue pages as well as lower paper prices. The planned reduction in advertising had the anticipated effect of lowering sales."
Inventory levels were "lower than optimum" during the third quarter because some manufacturers had problems delivering goods, he added.
"We believe this had an impact on sales as well. We look for improvements in this area in the fourth quarter," Thalheimer said.
San Francisco-based Sharper Image sells gifts and products through more than 90 stores in the United States and overseas, catalogues and other marketing channels.
Its stock was unchanged at $3.25 on Nasdaq in early afternoon trading.
